Subject: Sizing + pricing for Dedicated GPU pool (Haven Health)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. Quick context: we’re preparing to migrate inference for our medication-reconciliation and NLP summarization pipelines to a dedicated pool. Current profile: ~30 RPS steady-state across two services, with spikes up to ~120 RPS during business hours; average request spends ~1,000 tokens (prompt+response), peak contexts up to 6k tokens for some analysis jobs. Latency sensitivity: p95 < 600ms desirable for the user-facing flows.

Can you help with:
- Recommended GPU pool sizing (GPU type + count) for predictable throughput under the above workload, including headroom for bursts?
- Pricing for a 12-month reserved commit vs month-to-month, and any discount thresholds you can offer?
- Any tradeoffs if we accept quantized model builds or slightly smaller model variants?

Attaching a small workbook with daily RPS by endpoint and some sample traces.

Thanks,
James
VP Engineering | Haven Health

Hi James —

Appreciate the workbook — that helps a lot. A couple of quick clarifying q's before Marcus and I put numbers behind GPU counts:
1) Is the 120 RPS spike sustained concurrently across both services or concentrated in one?
2) Are there hard latency SLOs for administrative/analytics (the 6k token jobs) or are those batchy/off-peak?
3) Which model family are you planning to run in prod (open family / 13B-14B / our tuned variants)? That influences memory footprint and KV cache sizing.

Initial guidance off the top of my head: at ~1k tokens/request and 120 RPS peak you should plan for steady concurrency in the tens (we usually size for peak concurrency + 30% headroom). For dedicated pricing, we can propose a 12-month reserved commit with a tiered discount (we typically start at 18–22% on committed spend for this scale, with room to increase based on footprint and payment terms). Marcus — can you draft a technical sizing + cost sketch (GPU SKU options + expected throughput and fallback) so we can present numbers? Rishi — looping you for price approvals on discounts > 20%.

I’ll hold an hour tomorrow afternoon for a quick sizing review if that works for Haven.

Best,

James / Kimberly —

I took a pass on the workbook and sketched two pragmatic configurations with expected throughput numbers. Assumptions:
- Model: redwood-14b-open (float16) for user-facing flows; we can offer a q4_0 quantized build that cuts VRAM by ~35% with minor perf variance.
- Typical request: 1k tokens (512 prompt + 512 response); peak jobs up to 6k tokens (long-running, batch).
- Target latency: p95 < 600ms for 512-token responses.

Option A (balanced reliability + cost):
- GPU: 4 x H100-80GB (dedicated pool)
- Expected throughput: ~110–140 RPS for short 512-token responses with smart batching and KV cache enabled; sustains ~45 concurrent user-facing requests at our p95 target.
- Batch/long requests: schedule on separate node pool; 6k-token jobs run with prewarm and don't count toward user-facing pool.
- Autoscaling: keep baseline 3 GPUs with burst to 4 (burst buffer = 1 GPU).
- Pricing (12m reserved): estimated committed monthly spend $92,500 -> pre-discount.

Option B (cost-optimized with quantization):
- GPU: 3 x A800-80GB (or A100 equivalent) with q4_0 quant builds
- Expected throughput: ~80–100 RPS for typical 512-token responses; sustains ~30 concurrent user-facing requests reliably.
- Autoscaling: baseline 2 GPUs with burst to 3.
- Pricing (12m reserved): estimated committed monthly spend $64,800 -> pre-discount.

Notes / tradeoffs:
- If you accept quantized builds (q4_0) you can drop 20–30% on infra and still keep acceptable latency for most flows.
- We recommend isolating heavy batch jobs into a separate cheaper pool (preemptible or lower priority) to avoid interfering with p95 for user-facing traffic.
- We can include 2 months of free trial credits on new reserved commits for new enterprise customers.

I attached a short worksheet with the math and headroom calcs.

—Marcus

Kimberly / Marcus —

Thanks for the level of detail — helpful. Quick answers:
- Spikes are concentrated in the medication-reconciliation service (about 80% of the spike), the other service is fairly steady.
- The 6k-token jobs are largely offline analytics but do run daily in the morning window; they must complete within a 20-minute window but can be scheduled.
- We plan to run a 14B-class tuned model (not strict float16 baseline) — performance/payloads are around what you described.

Our ask: can you push pricing lower? We were budgeting ~$50k/month for committed reserved capacity. If we commit 12 months and can take quantized builds for non-critical endpoints, can we get to ~$50k–55k/mo? Also want to confirm you can guarantee p95 target (for user-facing flows) during spikes, and that batch jobs can be isolated so they don’t impact latency.

Appreciate a revised proposal with a possible staged rollout (start with 2 GPUs + canary, scale to target pool after 30 days).

-James

James —

We can get closer to your target with a packaging approach that balances guaranteed throughput and a committed spend floor. Here’s a commercial path we can offer:

Proposal (12-month reserved commit):
- Commit: $600k total annual = $50k/month effective commit.
- Discount: 25% off list on the reserved capacity price for that commit level.
- Trial: 2 months complimentary credits applied to early months (can be used for burst usage or batch runs).
- Throughput guarantee: We’ll include a Service Level Objective of 95% of user-facing requests served with p95 latency < 600ms measured over 30d rolling windows; remediation includes credits and capacity remediation plan.
- Isolation: Batch workloads run in a separate pool (we’ll provide orchestration + scheduling rules) — batch pool can be preemptible/cheaper.
- Canary: Start with 2-GPU canary for 30 days (integration + validation). After successful validation we shift to the committed pool size using usage signals.

Technical sizing recommendation (post-canary):
- Start: 2 x H100 (canary) + 1 x H100 burst reserve.
- Target: 4 x H100 for sustained peak headroom (or 3 x H100 + 1 x A800 hybrid to reduce cost if you accept quant builds on non-critical paths).

Conditions / asks:
- Payment terms: Net 30.
- Cancellation: pro-rated credits on unused months for early termination with 90-day notice.
- Negotiated discount >20% needs VP approval; Rishi has been looped and can confirm.

If this looks reasonable I’ll prepare a formal SOW and a DocuSign link for signatures.

—Marissa
